summary.text: Glenn Thompson is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 15th District. A Howard, Pennsylvania, native, he spent 28 years as a therapist, rehabilitation services manager and licensed nursing home administrator before his election to Congress in 2008. He has served since 2009 (the old 5th District through 2018) and chairs the House Committee on Agriculture.

paragraphs.text: Born in Howard, Pennsylvania, in 1959; his House website calls him a life-long resident of Howard.
Earned a bachelor's degree in therapeutic rehabilitation from Pennsylvania State University (1981) and a Master of Education from Temple University (1998).

Spent 28 years as a therapist, rehabilitation services manager and licensed nursing home administrator before his election to Congress, and has served as a volunteer firefighter for more than three decades, according to his House website.

Member of the Bald Eagle Area School Board (1990–1996); his House website also lists service as past vice-chair of the Private Industry Council of the Central Corridor and as a Workforce Investment Board member.

An Eagle Scout and 30-plus-year volunteer with the Juniata Valley Boy Scout Council (Scoutmaster, executive board member and Council President), he received the National Distinguished Eagle Scout Award in 2012.

Won the November 4, 2008 general election for Pennsylvania's 5th District, defeating Democrat Mark McCracken and Libertarian James Fryman, and took office in 2009; he has represented the 15th District since boundaries were redrawn in 2019.
Appointed to the House Committee on Education & Workforce in 2009 and now serves as a senior member; chairs the House Committee on Agriculture, per his House website.

Co-Chairman of the bipartisan Congressional Career and Technical Education Caucus for more than a decade; his House website says his Career and Technical Education for the 21st Century Act, introduced in the 115th Congress, passed the House and Senate unanimously and was signed into law.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Penny Ammerman-Thompson, have three adult sons and two grandsons, and live in Howard.
